## Rio Carnival and five countries in 19 days: what makes this journey special

This itinerary has a definite starting point: **Carnival in Rio de Janeiro and the Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome**. The private **19-day, 18-night** journey continues to Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires, Santiago de Chile, the Atacama Desert, the Uyuni Salt Flats, Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. It appeals to travelers who want to combine one of Brazil's best-known events with an extensive tour of South America.

Here, "Carnival" means **a real event included in the itinerary**. It is more than a free evening in town during the celebrations. Tickets for the Champions' Parade, in Sector 9 or a comparable sector, are included, along with **hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers**.

## Why departure dates must follow the Champions' Parade

The Champions' Parade takes place on a specific date in the Carnival calendar. That means the **actual event date and available departure** must be selected first, before international flights are arranged. The itinerary describes the Champions' Parade, but does not specify an exact tour departure date. Confirm this when agreeing on your departure instead of relying on the tour's name.

The first days in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) feature Sugarloaf Mountain, the historic center, Corcovado and Carnival itself. The Sambadrome visit takes place on a separate day. It must remain fixed when planning, even if other sightseeing stops can be rearranged: the event cannot be shifted to an arbitrary date.

If Carnival is not essential, compare the [18-day group tour through the same five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). That trip emphasizes a broad geographical route rather than a fixed Champions' Parade date.

## Both sides of Iguazu and the cultural sights of Argentina

After Rio, the journey proceeds to the [Brazilian side of Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The next stage visits the [Argentine side of the falls](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The Brazilian side gives panoramic views of the cascades; Argentine walkways take visitors closer to the water and the famous Devil's Throat. An international border crossing is required, so the two national parks are not one continuous walk.

Buenos Aires offers a city tour and an evening tango show with dinner. The exploration of South American traditions continues, now in a different city and musical setting. The route then passes through [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and moves from capital cities to deserts and high-altitude landscapes.

## Atacama, Uyuni and Titicaca: the challenging section

From Santiago the journey goes via Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Next comes a jeep route through Bolivia, with lagoons, volcanic landscapes, hot springs and geysers. After a night in the highlands, travelers visit the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), stopping at Colchani and Incahuasi Island.

The defining physical challenges are **altitude and long road journeys**. Parts of the plateau exceed 4,000 m, and facilities can be more basic than in city hotels. Assess your tolerance of high altitude before departure and speak to your doctor about any relevant medical restrictions. Weather can differ sharply from conditions in Rio.

After [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the route continues via Tiwanaku to Lake Titicaca, the Uros Islands and Peru. The final stage visits [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). This journey leaves little time for long, leisurely stays at each site: its strength is the sheer variety of places covered.

## Private format and actual inclusions

The trip is sold in a **private format**, but it includes **group excursions and shared transfers**. "Private" does not automatically mean a personal guide and exclusive vehicle on every leg. Refer to the program and agreed arrangements for each section.

The price covers accommodation, designated group excursions, guide services, domestic flights along the stated route, and Champions' Parade tickets with transfers to and from the Sambadrome. Russian-speaking guides are listed for Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, La Paz, the Cusco city tour and Lima. English-speaking guides accompany excursions in the Uyuni area, on Lake Titicaca and at Machu Picchu.

**International flights are excluded.** Optional excursions, food and drinks beyond the itinerary, personal expenses, tips and laundry are also extra. Compare the tour with the 18-day group option on more than duration alone: the Rio event and guiding arrangements matter as well.

## How to judge the pace and choose the best itinerary

The journey moves between humid tropics, major cities, arid Atacama and the cold high Andes. Pack for hot weather and chilly Andean nights. Since sections take place far from major cities, allow for long transfers and respect the planned sequence of domestic flights.

If your biggest dream is a Carnival evening but you would prefer a gentler journey afterward, consider the [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/). If Patagonia's glaciers interest you more than high-altitude Bolivia and Peru, the [12-day private Argentina and Brazil journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) may suit you better.

## Frequently asked questions about the five-country Carnival tour

### Which Carnival event is included?

The itinerary specifies the **Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome**, with tickets in Sector 9 or a comparable sector and transfers from the hotel and back. Confirm the event date for your particular departure.

### Are all excursions on this private tour exclusive?

No. Although the tour is classified as private, some excursions and transfers are listed as group services. Check the arrangements for each stage individually.

### Are flights between countries included?

The specified chain of domestic flights along the itinerary is included. International flights to the start of the trip and home again are paid for separately.

### Is Machu Picchu on the itinerary?

Yes. After Titicaca, the final section covers Cusco, a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and the journey's conclusion in Lima.

## Five Latin American countries in 18 days: who is this route for?

This group tour is for travelers ready to experience the Atlantic coast, tropical rainforest and the high Andes in a single trip. Over **18 days and 17 nights**, it moves through Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru in sequence. Its distinctive feature is extensive geography in limited time: city sightseeing alternates with flights, road transfers and excursions at altitude.

Early stops include [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and the [Brazilian side of Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), followed by the [Argentine side of the waterfalls](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Then comes [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), Bolivia's highland lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The journey ends via Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

## Where there is time to explore and where you have to move on

Brazil includes dedicated sightseeing days for Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the waterfalls. **Both sides of Iguazu** are included in the main itinerary: the Brazilian side offers an overall panorama of the cascades, while paths and boardwalks on the Argentine side bring you closer to the water. These are two different excursions through adjacent national parks separated by an international border.

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a city tour is combined with a tango show and dinner. A sightseeing route through [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) comes before the flight to Calama. The schedule is notably busy here, with little downtime between the cultural sights and the nature-focused portion of the trip.

The biggest change begins in Atacama. After [San Pedro](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), guests travel by off-road vehicle through highland Bolivia, visiting Laguna Verde, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers, Laguna Colorada and other lagoons. Later they cross the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and travel via [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and Tiwanaku toward Lake Titicaca.

In Peru, the trip between Puno and Cusco includes stops at historic sites. A full day is dedicated to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). This itinerary reveals several civilizations and natural zones, but remains busy until the flight out of Lima.

## Altitude and climate changes: the biggest preparation issue

Focus less on the tour's duration than on the **Chile–Bolivia–Peru section**. The route reaches approximately 3,800–4,400 m, and the overnight stay in the Bolivian desert is in simpler accommodation than in large cities. Mountain passes, hours in jeeps and nights on the plateau can be tiring even for experienced sightseeing travelers.

Bring clothes for a warm humid coast, the spray at Iguazu, cool evenings in Atacama and freezing highland conditions. Beachwear will not be sufficient for the whole journey. If you have an illness that altitude could aggravate, discuss the route with your doctor in advance. Everyone responds differently to high altitude.

The season at Uyuni matters too. In the dry season, the salt flat usually exposes its pale salt crust; after rain, portions may become reflective. **The mirror effect cannot be guaranteed on a specific day**: it depends on weather, and access to particular areas depends on road conditions.

## Group arrangements, flights and guide languages

The program includes **domestic flights**, group excursions, transfers with a driver and 17 nights' accommodation. Russian-speaking guidance is provided in Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, La Paz, Cusco and Lima. **English-speaking guides** accompany the excursions at Uyuni, Titicaca and Machu Picchu; Russian-speaking guidance for those stages can be arranged for an additional charge.

International flights to the start of the trip and home afterward are extra. Optional excursions, some meals, personal spending and tips are also outside the base package. When choosing a date, check not just the price but your arrival in Rio, departure from Lima and whether international flights align with the scheduled sequence of domestic flights.

## When another route may be better

For those specifically wishing to see the parade in Rio, there is a [19-day private five-country Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/). The Champions' Parade takes place on a fixed date and is a different reason to choose a departure. If glaciers and Tierra del Fuego followed by Iguazu and Rio sound more appealing, consider the [12-day private Argentina and Brazil journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/).

The attraction of this 18-day option is **maximum variety of landscapes and historic places in a group format**. If long city stays, fewer transfers or serious trekking matter more, look at focused [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) or [trips to Chile](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the five-country tour

### Are domestic flights included in this 18-day tour?

Yes, the domestic flights listed in the itinerary are included. International tickets and optional excursions are paid for separately under the program's terms.

### Will I have a Russian-speaking guide in Bolivia and at Machu Picchu?

In Uyuni, at Titicaca and at Machu Picchu the base program uses English-speaking guides. Russian-speaking guidance on these stages is available at extra cost; the main city stops have Russian-speaking guides.

### Are both sides of Iguazu Falls visited?

Yes. The itinerary includes excursions on the Brazilian and Argentine sides, so the international border crossing needs to be allowed for.

### Is the trip suitable for someone without high-altitude travel experience?

Mountaineering experience is not listed as necessary for ordinary sightseeing, but part of the route reaches about 3,800–4,400 m. Consider how well you tolerate altitude and discuss any medical restrictions before booking.

## A 19-day New Year tour of five Latin American countries: what matters when choosing

From **December 30, 2026, to January 17, 2027**, this itinerary visits Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The New Year celebration takes place on Copacabana Beach in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Then come Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires and Santiago. The second half of the journey includes high-altitude roads, the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Lake Titicaca, [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

The main difference from a shorter holiday trip is that **the two halves have very different conditions**. The first days feature a hot coastline and major cities, while the later stages include highlands, long journeys and several land borders. Nineteen days mean more than extra attractions: altitude preparation, clothing and documents all require attention.

## Five countries in one continuous sequence

| Stage | What happens during the tour |
| --- | --- |
| Brazil | Rio, New Year celebrations, two hilltop viewpoints and the Brazilian side of Iguazu |
| Argentina | Walkways on the Argentine side of Iguazu, Buenos Aires and tango |
| Chile | Santiago, a flight to Calama and San Pedro de Atacama |
| Bolivia | A 4×4 jeep tour through highland lagoons and Uyuni, then La Paz and Tiwanaku |
| Peru | Puno and Titicaca, the road to Cusco, Machu Picchu and the final stop in Lima |

This is a continuous 19-day program connecting neighboring countries by different means: flights, group transfers, 4×4 vehicles and a tourist coach. The number of countries alone tells only part of the story; the transfers between them and the number of nights at each stop matter more.

## Why New Year is at the start of the itinerary

The first four nights are in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Travelers arrive on December 30. On December 31 they visit Corcovado and celebrate New Year on Copacabana that evening. On January 1 they ascend Sugarloaf Mountain, followed by a free day on January 2.

This arrangement works well after a long flight: there is a night in a hotel before the celebration and some time to recover afterward. Copacabana is generally very crowded, so discuss how the New Year festivities and the return trip will be organized in advance. Independently booking a festive restaurant is not one of the tour's mandatory events.

On January 3 the group heads toward [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side of the falls offers panoramic views, while the Argentine side around [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) has walkways running among the cascades. The trip then continues to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

## The most demanding leg: crossing from Atacama into Bolivia

After Santiago there is a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Next, **4×4 vehicles** take travelers across the Chile–Bolivia border through lagoons, high-altitude desert and geothermal landscapes. On the second day of the jeep journey, travelers approach the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

Conditions here contrast sharply with Rio: cold nights, dry air, significant altitude and long drives far from large cities. Even without strenuous trekking, the highlands can be difficult to tolerate. Prepare warm layers over lighter clothing, allow for a gradual pace and seek individual medical advice if altitude affects any existing medical condition.

The itinerary allows for a Uyuni–La Paz flight or, if no flight is operating, an alternative overland journey described in that day's program. Discuss how changing airline schedules might affect the next stage instead of assuming that all connections are guaranteed.

## Peru: how Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu connect

After [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the itinerary passes the archaeological site of [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and crosses into Peru. A visit to the Uros Islands is included around [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). From there, travelers go by coach to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the base for the visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

This is a lengthy sequence that cannot be replaced by one short flight. Cities, transport and altitude change along the way. Check cabin luggage allowances for domestic flights and prepare the belongings you need for the overland mountain section. Entry to Machu Picchu depends on tickets for specific dates and visitor circuits; these arrangements must be checked when planning.

The final part takes place in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). After the highlands, travelers encounter another climate and a different program as they explore Peru's capital rather than salt flats and mountain roads.

## Documents, money and equipment for five countries

**Five countries mean five separate border jurisdictions.** Entry and transit requirements depend on citizenship, passport validity, flight itinerary and potential repeat border crossings. Ada Tours helps check the conditions for each traveler's particular route; a universal entry rule for all of Latin America would be misleading.

Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru have different national currencies. US dollars may be useful for certain payments, but their acceptance cannot be guaranteed in every town or at every stop. Discuss payment arrangements and cash reserves for remote locations while accounting for whether your specific bank card is usable.

Pack two sets of clothes: light clothing for the coast and warm, layered garments for the mountains. Comfortable shoes for Iguazu walkways, sun protection, a warm outer layer and a small daypack are important.

## Services and a comparison with a shorter tour

Included are group transfers and excursions, guides as specified, meals on designated days, stays in 4* or 5* hotels and the listed domestic flights. International flights and optional excursions are extra, as are meals not covered by the program.

If you primarily want a New Year celebration and three countries, compare the [10-day New Year tour through Brazil, Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-new-year-2027-10-days/). It is shorter and omits the Bolivian and Peruvian high-altitude section. Travelers interested in spending more time in Atacama can also compare the [15-day "Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama" route](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/).

## Frequently asked questions about the New Year route through five countries

### Can I skip the jeep tour in Bolivia?

The high-altitude 4×4 section is part of the main 19-day itinerary. Skipping it would require designing a different journey, not just rearranging an excursion.

### How long do we stay in Rio after New Year?

Before the flight to Iguazu, January 1 is a sightseeing day and January 2 is free.

### Are international flights included?

No. International air travel is expressly excluded. The domestic flights included in the package are listed in the itinerary itself.

### When should I discuss tolerance of high altitude?

Before booking and arranging flights, because this journey includes Atacama, the Bolivian Altiplano, La Paz and the Titicaca region. Anyone with medical limitations should decide with their doctor based on the actual heights and exertion involved.

## Five Latin American countries in 18 days: Carnival, Uyuni and Machu Picchu

This journey from **February 12 to March 1, 2027**, combines Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Over 18 days and 17 nights, the itinerary travels from the Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome to Bolivia's colorful lagoons and Uyuni Salt Flats, then continues to Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu.

This is a busy sightseeing tour with domestic flights, jeeps on the Altiplano and overland crossings between countries. The main reason to choose this 18-day journey is the chance to combine **a specific Carnival event** with natural and historic attractions in the Andes. Those looking for a relaxed trip with long stays in one city may find the pace too fast.

## Champions' Parade on February 13, 2027: the start in Rio

The first three days take place in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Highlights include a city tour, [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) and [Corcovado](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/). The central event is on the second day: **the Champions' Parade takes place on February 13, 2027**, a date matching the official LIESA calendar.

The tour includes tickets to the Sambadrome **in Sector 9 or an equivalent sector** and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers. This is what distinguishes the itinerary from ordinary February trips through Brazil: Carnival night is a confirmed part of the program. Final seating must be checked against the issued ticket.

The following days are spent at [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side gives panoramic views, while the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) features walkways close to the cascades. Travelers then continue to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) for a city tour and tango show.

## Visiting five countries without doubling back

| Days | Main stops |
| --- | --- |
| 1–3 | Rio and Carnival |
| 4–7 | Iguazu and Buenos Aires |
| 8–10 | Santiago and Atacama |
| 11–13 | Bolivia: lagoons, Uyuni, La Paz |
| 14–18 | Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu, Lima |

These are not five independent short excursions. Some borders are crossed by land and other sections by air. The most demanding leg starts after Santiago, as the Atacama Desert gives way to high-altitude Bolivia. The journey then enters Peru via Tiwanaku and Lake Titicaca.

## Chile and Bolivia: from the desert to the Altiplano

A city tour is included in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Next comes a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This region features desert landscapes, mountain ranges and astronomy-related experiences.

On day 11 the group drives to the Bolivian border and switches to jeeps. The route passes Laguna Verde, the Salvador Dalí Desert, Polques hot springs, Sol de Mañana geysers and Laguna Colorada. On the next day, the jeep itinerary heads toward the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and Incahuasi Island. On day 13, a flight takes the group to La Paz.

The conditions are particularly different from Rio: hours on the road, major changes in altitude, cold mornings and limited comfort at some remote overnight stops. **One night is spent in a basic hotel in the desert.** It would be misleading to judge this stage only by the hotel categories in large cities.

## Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu

Peru comes after Tiwanaku and the journey to Lake Titicaca. Puno and the Uros Islands are included. Travelers then go toward Cusco via Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, Sicuani and the La Raya Pass.

Day 16 features a group excursion to Machu Picchu with an **English-speaking guide**. The following day covers Cusco's attractions, including Qorikancha and Sacsayhuamán, followed by a flight to Lima. The final day features Lima's sights and the Larco Museum.

Access to Machu Picchu is regulated: entry, routes within the site and visiting times all depend on confirmed tickets. Plan this excursion around the other transfers rather than assuming that any day will be available.

## What guide services and flights are included

The itinerary provides **Russian-speaking guides** in Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago, La Paz, on the Cusco city tour and in Lima. **English-speaking guides** accompany the Uyuni, Titicaca and Machu Picchu excursions. It would be inaccurate to describe the entire journey as guided in Russian.

The package includes hotels specified in the program, excursions, designated transfers with a driver, Champions' Parade tickets and **domestic flights on the route** as listed. International flights, optional excursions, meals not specified, tips and personal spending are paid separately.

Prices **start at $9562 per person** for **double occupancy in 4★ hotels**. SGL/DBL/TPL arrangements are available for both 4★ and 5★ categories; preserve the selected hotel category and room configuration when comparing costs.

## Preparing for major changes in altitude

The first days are spent in the warm lowlands of Brazil, but the Altiplano and Andes require different equipment. Bring warm wind-resistant clothing, sun protection, closed shoes and a small daypack for jeep outings. Dust and bumpy roads on the Bolivian leg differ greatly from city sightseeing.

**Altitude is a key consideration.** La Paz, Uyuni, the mountain lagoons and the route along Titicaca lie far above Rio and Buenos Aires. Seek individual medical advice before traveling if you have health problems that altitude could affect. Entry requirements and access to attractions in five countries should be checked against citizenship, specific dates and every planned border crossing.

The [multi-country routes catalog](/multi-country/) includes trips with fewer countries and flights. This 18-day journey is especially suitable for those who want **the Champions' Parade, Bolivia's high-altitude landscapes and Peru's historical treasures in one trip**.

## Frequently asked questions about the five-country tour

### What date is the Champions' Parade scheduled for?

**February 13, 2027**, the second day of the itinerary. Sambadrome tickets and return transfers are included.

### Are all guides Russian-speaking?

No. Russian-speaking guides are provided at cities and selected stops, but at Uyuni, Titicaca and Machu Picchu the guides speak English.

### Are domestic flights included?

Yes. The flights specified within the itinerary are included. International flights cost extra.

### Is a high-altitude section included?

Yes. Chile's Atacama Desert, the Bolivian Altiplano, Uyuni and the Titicaca region all form substantial parts of the trip. Consider this when assessing how well you can cope physically.

## Argentina Deluxe in 11 days: Buenos Aires, Patagonia, Ushuaia and Iguazu

The **11-day, 10-night** itinerary covers four main areas: [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and nearby [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), and Iguazu Falls, visited from both [Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/).

**The tour genuinely includes two main countries: Argentina and Brazil.** There is also an optional day trip to Uruguay, but it is a choice for a free day rather than part of the guaranteed route.

Deluxe arrangements include 5-star hotels, private transfers with a driver in a Mercedes Vito or similar vehicle, and guided excursions. It is a convenient way to combine a historic capital, southern glaciers and subtropical waterfalls in one organized journey.

## Buenos Aires: city tour, tango and a free day

The first three days are spent in Argentina's capital. The proposed hotel is **Four Seasons Buenos Aires**. Day two includes a city tour and an evening **Gala Tango** event, with dinner and transfers.

The inclusions require careful reading: **dinner and transfers for Gala Tango** are specifically listed, while the price of the actual show is excluded and quoted **"on request"**. Confirm the exact services covered by your selected package before booking rather than assuming that every show ticket is paid for.

Day three is free. Optional choices include a trip to Tigre and San Isidro, a ranch with a gaucho program, or a ferry journey to [Colonia del Sacramento in Uruguay](/uruguay/). These are alternatives; **all three excursions are not included together** on the same free day.

## El Calafate and Perito Moreno Glacier

On day four, a flight brings the group to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), with accommodation at **Eolo Patagonia's Spirit Lodge** in a Superior Room with full board. Day five features Los Glaciares National Park and [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/).

From the observation walkways visitors can watch the glacier's enormous walls of ice. Pieces may break off naturally, but not on a schedule, so no particular calving moment can be promised. **Trekking directly on the ice is an optional extra**, not an automatic part of the sightseeing visit.

This section's great attraction is the chance to see the glacier in the national park and spend time amid Patagonia's mountain scenery while retaining comfortable accommodation between sightseeing days.

## Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego National Park

On day six, the itinerary continues to [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) in southern Argentina. The hotel list specifies **Arakur Ushuaia**, Superior Room with breakfast. Day seven is devoted to [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), including its coastline, lakes, forests and southern landscapes.

The sea excursion to [Martillo Island](/argentina/place/martillo-island/) to watch penguins is **optional**. It must be arranged separately, and sightings cannot be guaranteed outside the appropriate season and visiting conditions.

The climate and scenery change repeatedly on this tour. Warm windproof clothing is essential for Patagonia even though the later itinerary reaches the hot Iguazu region.

## Iguazu: two countries and two very different views

On day eight the journey moves to Iguazu, with accommodation specified at **Belmond Hotel das Cataratas**, in a Deluxe Room with breakfast. Day nine visits the [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), where broad views of the falls open up against subtropical forest.

Day ten covers the [Argentine side near Puerto Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) with walks along several routes, including the famous Devil's Throat if that section is accessible. The trip then returns to Buenos Aires; day eleven is the flight home.

The Brazilian and Argentine Iguazu national parks are both UNESCO World Heritage sites. Crossing between them requires attention to entry formalities based on the traveler's nationality. **Macuco Safari**, the Bird Park and a helicopter flight are listed as optional activities, rather than mandatory paid services.
